rationale: No tensors in this template can reproduce every demonstration. In the first demonstration, background pixels (4,1) and (4,2), indexed from zero, have identical nearest-colour keys but different outputs. The other key kinds likewise merge pixels requiring different outputs; none encodes the required displacement distances.

Pixel count distinguishes the demonstrated large objects and maps the small marker objects to zero, reproducing the supplied demonstrations when all are context. Generalisation to unseen object sizes is unsupported: the intended recolouring depends on the separate marker's shape, which this template cannot access.

No solution exists within object_table. It only recolours existing components and leaves background cells unchanged. The expected outputs introduce coloured pixels at previously empty positions outside the frame.

No solution exists within neighbor_table. The outputs depend on connectivity along the corridor and the marker's position. The available local keys merge pixels requiring different outputs; changing background cannot supply that missing connectivity information.

No solution exists within neighbor_table. In the third demonstration, pixels (3,2) and (3,6) have identical neighbourhoods but require outputs 8 and 9 respectively. Their neighbour counts and colour sets also coincide, ruling out every available key kind.

No solution exists within ray_cast. Source colours must paint their own crosses, while intersections must become colour 2. The template has no intersection rule: source-colour painting cannot create 2 here, and fixed paint colour 2 would incorrectly recolour entire rays.
